attachments.origin_landmark: humeral head: lateral epicondyle; ulnar head: posterior ulna

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population (2 heads sharing one belly)
functional_compartments.function_note: Runs in its own fibro-osseous groove on the distal ulna, stabilized by a subsheath of the extensor retinaculum -- a common site of tendinopathy/subluxation ('ECU snapping') in racquet sports.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Probe placed longitudinally (long axis) over the most ulnar of the extensor-mass muscle bellies on the dorsomedial forearm, localized by palpation distal to the lateral epicondyle/olecranon while the patient performs resisted wrist extension combined with ulnar deviation.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial extensor compartment, most ulnar of the common-extensor-origin muscles, running distally in its own groove on the ulnar head/distal ulna.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Contracts selectively with resisted wrist extension plus ulnar deviation (distinguishing it from ECRL/ECRB, which deviate radially); tracks the ulnar border of the forearm down to its groove on the distal ulna.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: One of four muscles injected under ultrasound guidance (10-30 U incobotulinumtoxinA/muscle, split site if muscle bulk requires it) in a clinical series treating chronic lateral epicondylitis; injections were placed at the muscle's motor end plate region under long-axis probe view, localized first by palpation from the epicondyle during resisted contraction. This is a pain/overuse-treatment context rather than post-stroke spasticity, but the sonographic localization technique is the same. ECU was the least frequently symptomatic of the four muscles in that series (29.2% of patients).
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Galvan Ruiz A, Vergara Diaz G, Rendon Fernandez B, Echevarria Ruiz de Vargas C, 'Effects of Ultrasound-Guided Administration of Botulinum Toxin (IncobotulinumtoxinA) in Patients with Lateral Epicondylitis', Toxins 11(1):46 (2019), doi:10.3390/toxins11010046 (https://doi.org/10.3390/toxins11010046) -- retrieved via PubMed
